actions.diff:
--- a/base58/__init__.py
+++ b/base58/__init__.py
@@ -80,8 +80,12 @@
-) -> Tuple[List[bytes], int, int, int, bytes]:
-    # Everything b58encode needs per alphabet: the digit pair table, the
-    # pair base (base**2), the divisor (base**4), base**12 and the zero
-    # character
-    sq = len(alphabet) ** 2
-    big = sq * sq
-    return (_get_base58_encode_pairs(alphabet), sq, big, big ** 3,
-            alphabet[0:1])
+) -> Tuple[List[bytes], List[bytes], int, int, int, int, int, bytes]:
+    # Everything b58encode needs per alphabet: the digit pair table, the
+    # single digit table, the pair base (base**2), base**4, the tail
+    # divisor (base**4), the bulk divisor (base**5, which still fits in
+    # one internal int digit), base**20 and the zero character
+    base = len(alphabet)
+    sq = base * base
+    big = sq * sq
+    big5 = big * base
+    ones = [alphabet[d:d + 1] for d in range(base)]
+    return (_get_base58_encode_pairs(alphabet), ones, sq, big, big5,
+            big5 ** 4, alphabet[0:1])

--- a/base58/__init__.py
+++ b/base58/__init__.py
@@ -140,13 +140,13 @@
-    pairs, sq, big, big3, zero = tables
-    parts = []
-    while i >= big3:
-        # Four groups of four digits per pass while at least four remain
-        i, rem = divmod(i, big)
-        i, rem2 = divmod(i, big)
-        i, rem3 = divmod(i, big)
-        i, rem4 = divmod(i, big)
-        # rem is a small int: two operators are cheaper than a divmod call
-        parts += (pairs[rem % sq], pairs[rem // sq],
-                  pairs[rem2 % sq], pairs[rem2 // sq],
-                  pairs[rem3 % sq], pairs[rem3 // sq],
-                  pairs[rem4 % sq], pairs[rem4 // sq])
+    pairs, ones, sq, big, big5, big20, zero = tables
+    parts = []
+    while i >= big20:
+        # Four groups of five digits per pass while at least four remain;
+        # each group is two digit pairs and one single digit
+        i, rem = divmod(i, big5)
+        i, rem2 = divmod(i, big5)
+        i, rem3 = divmod(i, big5)
+        i, rem4 = divmod(i, big5)
+        parts += (pairs[rem % sq], pairs[rem // sq % sq], ones[rem // big],
+                  pairs[rem2 % sq], pairs[rem2 // sq % sq], ones[rem2 // big],
+                  pairs[rem3 % sq], pairs[rem3 // sq % sq], ones[rem3 // big],
+                  pairs[rem4 % sq], pairs[rem4 // sq % sq], ones[rem4 // big])

journal.text:
I read base58/__init__.py and lineage_bench.py. Then I edited the encode path in three places. The first edit replaced 8 lines with 12 near line 80. The second touched lines 140-152. The third revised lines 82-84. Same bytes out was the bar.

The bytes held. Equivalence came back with identical outputs, and the guard was ok at 1 file and 40 lines. The speed did not hold. encode_ir went from 218502715 to 221541306, a ratio of 1.0139. The required ratio was 0.9900, so it was rejected for no improvement. decode_ir rose to ratio 1.0080. check_ir rose to ratio 1.0158. Everything got a little slower. I did not submit a candidate.

What I believe now is narrow. My rewrite added work per call instead of removing it. I do not yet know which of the three edits cost the most. Not measured yet.

Next I will revert to the parent. Then I will apply one edit at a time and run encode_ir after each, starting with lines 80-87.
